title: This 600-Year-Old Wall Took 350 Million Bricks — Each One Signed | China Travel Expert
description:
Forget the Great Wall for a second. The longest, best-preserved ancient city wall on Earth wraps a single city — Nanjing — and it hides a genius secret.

Built between 1366 and 1386 by the first Ming emperor, Zhu Yuanzhang, the wall ran 35.3 km around the capital — the longest city wall in the world. Some 200,000 workers laid roughly 350 million bricks in about two decades. Here's the clever part: every brick was stamped with the county it came from, the official who supervised it, and the name of the individual who made it. If a stretch ever crumbled, they knew exactly whose brick failed — an early quality-control system, and today the biggest surviving set of construction records anywhere. About 21 km still stands, averaging 12 meters tall.

🧭 Expert Tip: Walk the Zhonghua Gate (中华门) section — its fortress-like inner courtyards and hidden troop chambers, said to hold thousands of soldiers, are the most impressive part of the whole wall.

世界最长的古城墙不在别处——它绕着南京，而且每块砖都刻着造砖人的名字。
